steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease a 12-cup muffin tin or line with paper liners.
Combine flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl.
Stir in chocolate chips, milk, melted butter, and egg until batter is combined.
Pour batter into the prepared muffin cups.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center of a muffin comes out clean, 15 to 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Basic Chocolate Chip Muffins
raw_recipe.description: These easy chocolate chip muffins are tender, moist, and come together in a jiffy, with a liberal helping of chocolate chips studded throughout.
raw_recipe.name: Basic Chocolate Chip Muffins

review.reviewBody: This recipe is so good! It def hits any sweet tooth! The changes I made were: 2 c flour, 1 tbsp baking powder, 1 c sugar and a splash of vanilla. They were perfect! I also added a few chocolate chips to the top before baking at 400 for 20 min. They were golden brown & delicious! I will def make this again.

I made them but added a tsp of vanilla. My batter was wet but I figured it was because of the vanilla. Then I put them in the oven and read the reviews and saw other people had the same problem and someone suggested bumping up the heat. I quickly went and turned it up to 375 and they came out perfect.

The ratios are off on this recipe. With a full cup of milk, there isn’t enough sugar to brown the muffins or enough flour to support the weight of the chocolate chips. It does make an edible muffin, but they’re pale and pancake-like instead of muffin-like. Suggested fixes: bring sugar up to 2/3 cup (mixing brown and white is good for flavor), add another 1/4-1/2 cup flour, bring milk down to 1/3-1/2 cup, add 1 teaspoon vanilla. Bake at 375 instead of 350, 18-20 minutes.

This recipe (with the added tweaks and adjustments that is) came out great. I followed the suggestions of adding 2 cups of flour, 1 cup of sugar and 1 tbsp of baking powder. I also used a quarter cup of vegetable oil instead of butter. The batter was thick and rich and baked up perfectly at 350 for 18 minutes. They do tend to be a bit more pale in color but they really are fluffy and delicious.

These turned out terrific! I did use the suggested changes of 2 cups flour, 1cup sugar and vanilla. I also topped them after baking with melted butter and a mixture 3tbsp white sugar & 2tbsp brown sugar sprinkled on top.

I used some tapioca starch and a dash of cornstarch to accommodate my egg allergy, used carob chips instead of chocolate (also allergic) and added some dried cherries. I added some carob powder, and also had to add about 2/3c extra flour because the batter was extremely runny with the given proportions. 

They turned out nicely! I agree with the others who talked about them being rather pale and bland if you don't tweak the recipe a bit, but after adjustment they're good. I feel like this is a good basic recipe for people who want a jumping off point to explore their own flavor combinations.

Not bad. I'm not a huge chocolate fan so 1 cup of chocolate chips was too much for my taste. I'll try 3/4 cup next time. Definitely spray muffin tins with a non stick spray. My other muffin recipe doesn't stick to the liners, so I didn't see a need for that step. I was wrong. They didn't rise much so may add 1/2 cup more flour next time. I didn't think about vanilla until after they were in the oven, so that might make it even better next time. These did not brown. I left them in an extra 3 minutes, then 2 minutes, then another 2 minutes thinking they'd brown a little. I finally just took them out and tested with a toothpick. The color was almost the same as the batter.

I made this today but changed a few things. The batter tasted too floury so I added a teaspoon of vanilla and a large pinch of additional sugar. I also added a cup of chopped strawberries! Baked for the full 20 min and they are fabulous!
Good recipe. I made mine in a loaf pan and used 1 1/2 cup flour, 1/2 cup cocoa and 1 Tbsp baking powder. Baked at 350 for roughly 40 minutes.

This recipe is simple and perfect! I didn't read all the reviews but it seems a couple people said there was too much liquid. I followed the recipe with two exceptions. I added 1/2 tsp of vanilla and I didn't melt the butter. I added the butter to the mixer at room temperature. Could solve peoples "liquid" issues. They were perfect. I baked at 350 for 12 minutes and then 250 for 7 minutes. So much less expensive than 20 mini hostess muffins with a whole lot of preservatives for $4.99 a box. Gotta love home-made! Thank you Julia!
A very quick, easy and delicious recipe. I soaked a cup of rolled oats in the cup of milk (to soften them) for about 15 minutes before adding it in to the mixture.

I can't decide between 4 & 3 stars. They were really easy to make, but many people are right about them tasting more like pancakes. All the chocolate chips sunk to the bottom. They didn't really rise or brown. It definitely could have used some vanilla. But other than that, they are fine. A good recipe if you are really in a pinch, but I feel like I kind of wasted a good stick of butter. 😬 Sadly, I won't be adding this one to my recipe book.
Absolutely no a scam I recommend you try those majestic muffins they are perfect I was amazed I now bake them every day
They just taste so goood

Made these with my 6yo GD- she loved them, and so did the rest of us! Very easy to make, and I liked that it was a 12 muffin batch so we aren't picking at them for days. agree with suggestion to toss chips in flour to prevent sinking - but GD liked the lava like surprise in the middle. We are already planning the next baking day!

I absolutely loved this recipe!!! I used the technique to add 2cups of flour and 1cup of sugar and just a splash of vanilla extract 😀 The recipe made 12 muffins and at the end of the day we ended up with only 2 left so they were definitely delicious 😋 I think you should really use this recipe

i halfed the recipe but used a whole egg instead of half, pistachio milk in place of cow's milk, and i added some cinnamon, allspice, and cocoa powder for flavor. these were delicious, i didnt have an issue with them sticking to the muffin cups as others described. id definitely make these again as theyre so simple and so good.
I made no changes and they came out great!
It’s easy to prepare with some ingredients we have at home. 15min is good, but we add 3min to make them top brown.

Its really easy and tasty but pale when you cook it for the time it gives. My toothpick was clean but the muffins looked practically white. I left it in for a little longer until it was golden brown. They tasted great, but the only flavor was the chocolate. I probably won't use this recipe again, but it was worth a try. This would be good to take to a party because it's one of the least offensive-tasting foods. It would be hard to not like it.
